entry.title: SimCity's Performance Optimization Techniques for 16 MHz Hardware Examined
entry.content:
Links: larstofus.com | discussion | hacker news

The article examines how early development teams successfully ran complex simulation games like the original 1989 SimCity on constrained 16 MHz hardware. By analyzing the open-source Micropolis codebase, the piece highlights how core simulation systems—such as traffic, fire, and crime—were updated across multiple frames rather than all at once every frame.

This technique of distributing computational workloads across frames avoids performance bottlenecks without noticeably degrading gameplay responsiveness. The author notes that similar frame-budgeting principles extend to modern graphics and rendering pipelines, such as reflection cubemaps in Assetto Corsa and dynamic lighting in Unreal Engine.

Project Hedra is an open-world, low-poly 3D role-playing game paired with a custom game engine built completely from scratch. It features procedurally generated infinite worlds, quest systems, character classes, skill trees, and a modern OpenGL rendering pipeline.

Developed initially by maxilevi while in high school to learn computer graphics, the codebase spans approximately 100,000 lines of C#. The custom engine incorporates advanced technical features including runtime shader reloading, IronPython-based modding support, custom memory allocators to minimize garbage collection, and an entity component system.

entry.title: Isaac Marovitz Examines Unused Visual Features and Rendering Systems in Sonic 06
entry.content:
Links: isaacmarovitz.com | discussion

Developer Isaac Marovitz explores the technical reasons behind the downgraded visuals of Sonic the Hedgehog (2006), detailing how performance constraints during crunch led Sonic Team to disable advanced shaders, shadow map cascades, and point lights. Through work on the Marathon Recompiled project, the analysis reveals that many higher-fidelity visual assets and effects from beta builds remain dormant in the game files.

The article examines specific rendering limitations, such as the widespread reliance on rudimentary vertex-lit shaders like Billboard02, unoptimized point light counts that overload specific stages, and disabled real-time planar reflections in multiplayer modes. While some of these systems can be tweaked or stabilized via recompilation and patching, swapping core shader variants remains challenging due to complex material definitions and input layouts.
